title: Consistent Hashing
description: A cache cluster uses one random ring position per server. Some servers own far more keys than others, and membership changes are expected. Which statement points to an appropriate placement improvement?

options.text: When a node is added to a consistent hash ring, all keys must be redistributed
options.explanation: A joining node takes its neighboring ranges. Adding one equal-capacity node to N existing balanced nodes moves about K/(N+1) keys on average, where K is total keys. Modulo rehashing instead remaps most keys.

options.text: Virtual nodes help solve the problem of uneven key distribution across physical nodes
options.explanation: Multiple ring positions per physical node reduce random ownership skew by giving it many small ranges. This improves the expected key distribution; it does not guarantee equal bytes, request rates or hot-key load.

options.text: Consistent hashing guarantees perfectly equal load distribution
options.explanation: Even with virtual nodes, consistent hashing only provides approximately equal distribution. Perfect equality would require dynamic rebalancing based on actual load, not just key count.

options.text: Consistent hashing is only used for cache distribution
options.explanation: Ring-style placement appears in Dynamo's design, Cassandra token ranges, distributed caches, some load balancers, CDNs and file systems. Do not assume DynamoDB's internal layout is a textbook ring.
